alex.nguyen: fyi - ACME reported a >50% drop in embeddings vectors/sec starting ~0700 UTC yesterday. tokens/sec looks fine, but vector throughput and p95 are up. seeing queue depth spikes on the embeddings pool. attaching quick notes.

sam.k: which endpoint + model? any errors returned to client?

alex.nguyen: embeddings-v1 (customer endpoint). model=openembed-3-small, dim=1536. customer sends batches of ~64 short texts (avg 12 tokens). clients see 200 OK but vectors/sec down, and our per-request latency p95 for embed calls jumped 2x. no consistent 5xxs, a few 429s during the spike window.

priya.r: can you paste the minimal repro curl? also, any recent rollout to the embeddings pool?

alex.nguyen: repro (sanitized):
```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/embeddings \
  -d '{"model":"openembed-3-small","input":["short sentence"]*64}'\
```
ran against the customer's region and we see client RTT ~120ms but server-side queue time jumps to 800-1200ms during the dip.

maria.eng: quick signal dump I pulled: GPU util on pod set A rose to 95% (nice) but kernel_run_time shows tailing stalls. batcher queue depth PromQL:
```
sum(rate(embeddings_batcher_queue_depth[1m])) by (pool)
```
shows a sharp step at 0700 UTC. KV cache miss-rate also increased ~3x.

sam.k: KV cache miss -> repeated recompute of prefix? but these are single-pass embed requests (no chat kv). odd. any batching config changes?

alex.nguyen: infra configs unchanged. customer volume steady. spike correlates with a customer-side traffic pattern change (they started many concurrent small requests via parallel workers).

maria.eng: plausible. small concurrent requests -> more small batches -> lower tokens/sec efficiency and higher per-vector overhead. but that usually lowers cost efficiency, not GPU stalls. can you grep logs for "kernel stall" and "cuCtxSynchronize" around the spike?

alex.nguyen: logs:
```
WARN embeddings.batch: queue_depth=4096 -> 16384 at 2026-03-15T07:03:21Z
ERROR runtime.gpu: kernel_launch failed: CU_ERR_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT (retrying)
WARN runtime.kv: miss_rate=0.72 (baseline 0.21)
```
no OOMs.

priya.r: customer also reported intermittent 429s — could be our rate limiter bumping because batcher queue grows and we cap inflight to protect SLOs. any bump in per-route concurrency limits?

maria.eng: I checked routing config — no recent change. Hypothesis: a downstream microburst from a partner service caused request clustering which overloaded a subset of replicas. When queue depth jumped, our backpressure kicks in and we return 429 to upstream to shed. Also the kernel_launch timeouts indicate a possible driver-level contention on that instance class.

eng-oncall-bot: scheduled canary: reduced max_batch_items from 128 -> 64 on pool embeddings-prod-1 at 2026-03-15T08:10Z (10% traffic), enabled strict batching_timeout_ms=15.

maria.eng: nice. please run a controlled repro: 1) send 10k parallel one-sentence requests (client concurrency 200) 2) measure queue_depth and gpu_util 3) rerun with reduced max_batch_items and lowered batching timeout.

alex.nguyen: did that shortly after canary. results: with default config queue_depth peaked 12k, gpu_util 94%, kernel stalls seen. with reduced batch cap + timeout queue_depth peak ~2k, gpu_util 78%, p95 latency improved 35%, vectors/sec recovered ~40%.

sam.k: that suggests long batching windows combined with many tiny requests were creating large batches that, paradoxically, caused longer kernel runs and increased contention. smaller batches reduced tail even if slightly worse token-per-second efficiency. good trade for latency-sensitive customers.

priya.r: customer update: they can throttle client concurrency temporarily. recommended fix: set client-side concurrency cap OR we'll offer an endpoint config tuned for low-latency (we can give them an "embeds-low-latency" variant with lower max_batch_items).

maria.eng: long-term fixes: 1) make batching policy adaptive by detecting many small requests and switch to latency-first mode, 2) add kernel-level watchdog to preempt straggler kernels, 3) improve KV cache warmup for short-text distributions.

alex.nguyen: quick note — also found a small fraction (~0.6%) of requests had dim mismatch (client sending precomputed vectors mistakenly), causing a different codepath to run on CPU and increase load on other replicas. filtered those at edge; that reduced odd spikes.

eng-oncall-bot: rolled the canary to 50% at 2026-03-15T09:25Z. monitoring key signals.

maria.eng: next steps: 1) keep canary until 12h with metrics: vectors/sec, queue_depth, kernel_launch_timeouts 2) ship a short-run docs note for customers about client concurrency patterns and suggested client caps 3) backlog work for adaptive batching.

alex.nguyen: closing loop with ACME; they accepted using our low-latency variant and throttled client concurrency. we'll keep thread open until canary finishes. :thumbsup:

sam.k: thanks all.

infra-bot: alert cleared: embeddings-prod-1 queue_depth normalized at 2026-03-15T11:02Z

alex.nguyen: marking this as resolved from support side unless any objections.

maria.eng: ack, filing follow-up ticket ENG-4578 to track adaptive batching and KV warmup improvements.

priya.r: tagging account team to do customer follow-up tomorrow. :email:
